title: A Ghost for the Asset
premise: Sebastian Yarrow, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Section — an embassy that exists on no map — is haunted by a botched extraction he can't remember clearly. When a woman named Ilse Varga repays a favor he has no record of doing, she drags him into a conspiracy: the Section itself trained the network now selling its own assets to hostile buyers. To survive, Sebastian must burn his handlers, expose the training program, and choose between the identity they built for him and the truth of who he was before. In the end, he torches the Section's archive, hands the evidence to a journalist, and walks away as a man with no country and, for the first time, no debt.
about_author: Cyrus Thackeray is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent eleven years in postings he still cannot name. He writes thrillers from a coastal town where, he insists, nothing ever happens.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Sebastian Yarrow, sleepless and precise, works a routine cleanup job in Vienna when a stranger, Ilse Varga, approaches him claiming he saved her life in Prague two years ago. He has no memory of it. Her certainty unsettles him more than her threat. POV: Sebastian. Beat: unease — the first crack in his controlled world.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse explains the debt: someone in the Section marked her for disposal, and only Sebastian's name kept her alive. She wants him to find out why. He refuses, then finds a Prague entry in his own redacted file that shouldn't exist. POV: Sebastian. Beat: denial curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: Meridian Section
chapters.summary: Sebastian's handler, Director Calloway, dismisses his questions about Prague and reassigns him to surveillance duty — a soft exile. Sebastian notices Calloway's assistant quietly pulling his file. POV: Sebastian. Beat: the institution he trusted begins to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Ilse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV: she is not what she seems — a former asset from the same training program, codename LARK, who escaped. She keeps a ledger of names: everyone the program trained, everyone it erased. She chose Sebastian because his name appears twice. Beat: revelation reframes everything; sympathy deepens.

chapters.title: Two Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian digs into his past and finds a second identity — 'Daniel Reeve' — with service records predating his recruitment. The Section didn't hire him; it manufactured him. POV: Sebastian. Beat: vertigo of lost self; grief for a life he can't recall.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Rule
chapters.summary: An old contact is found dead in a Meridian safehouse, staged as suicide. Sebastian recognizes the staging — he invented the technique. Someone is using his own methods against his circle. POV: Sebastian. Beat: fear becomes personal; the hunter realizes he is prey.

chapters.title: Lisbon Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Ilse and Sebastian meet a retired trainer, Moreau, in Lisbon who confirms the program 'Chrysalis' existed: building assets with implanted backstories and loyalty triggers. Moreau agrees to testify, then vanishes before the meeting ends. POV: alternating. Beat: hope raised and snatched away; rising stakes.

chapters.title: Trigger
chapters.summary: Sebastian experiences a dissociative episode — a phrase overheard in a café sends him executing trained protocols he never consciously learned. Ilse witnesses it and pulls him out. POV: Sebastian, fragmented. Beat: horror at his own wiring; Ilse becomes his anchor.

chapters.title: Calloway's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Confronting Calloway, Sebastian gets half an admission: Chrysalis was sanctioned above the Section, and the 'incident' that broke his sleep was a test gone wrong. Calloway warns him to stop. POV: Sebastian. Beat: partial truth; the enemy has layers.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Ilse traces Chrysalis-trained assets being auctioned to a broker called Ferenc Halas. Surveillance reveals a sale scheduled in ten days — inside Meridian's own annex. The network isn't leaking; it's headquartered here. POV: Ilse. Beat: cold clarity; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Sleepless in the Annex
chapters.summary: Sebastian infiltrates the annex archives at night and photographs Chrysalis rosters — and finds his own trigger phrase documented, along with orders for his termination once the sale completes. POV: Sebastian. Beat: betrayal fully lands; survival now requires war.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Sebastian recruits two disaffected Section staff — analyst Priya Nair and comms officer Dekker — risking their lives on his word alone. Trust is tested when Dekker hesitates. POV: Priya. Beat: fragile alliance; loyalty weighed against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Moreau's Grave
chapters.summary: They find Moreau dead in a Lisbon canal. Among his effects: a key to a Chrysalis off-site facility in the Carpathians. Ilse admits she's been there before — it's where she broke. POV: Ilse. Beat: mourning and resolve braided together.

chapters.title: The Carpathian Facility
chapters.summary: The pair infiltrates the decommissioned-but-active training site and finds current subjects — including a boy being conditioned with Sebastian's original case file as template. POV: Sebastian. Beat: moral rupture; this is no longer about him.

chapters.title: What Daniel Knew
chapters.summary: In the facility's records, Sebastian recovers footage of Daniel Reeve volunteering — he wasn't kidnapped; he enlisted to escape something worse, and Chrysalis exploited it. POV: Sebastian. Beat: painful self-knowledge; identity reclaimed through choice, not erasure.

chapters.title: Ilse's Price
chapters.summary: Ilse confesses her real motive: her brother is among the sold assets, alive in Halas's custody. She used Sebastian's guilt as leverage. He forgives her — or decides to. POV: Ilse. Beat: betrayal and grace; loyalty vs. truth made intimate.

chapters.title: Calloway's Choice
chapters.summary: Calloway, cornered by Sebastian's evidence, defects partially — revealing the sale's date moved up to tomorrow and naming the deputy director, Vance, as Chrysalis's architect. Calloway buys them hours with his career. POV: Calloway. Beat: an antagonist becomes tragic; institutions devour their own.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Vance triggers Sebastian's conditioning remotely during a public event, turning him into a weapon aimed at Ilse. She uses his true name — Daniel — as a counter-anchor, breaking the protocol. POV: both, interleaved. Beat: climax begins; love and truth defeat programming.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: They storm the annex auction, freeing the caged assets including Ilse's brother, while Priya streams the Chrysalis files to journalists worldwide. Dekker dies holding the door. POV: Priya. Beat: costly victory; sacrifice gives the truth weight.

chapters.title: Vance's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts Vance, who offers him restoration — his records, his old life, reinstated. Sebastian refuses and lets Vance be taken by the very oversight bodies he corrupted. POV: Sebastian. Beat: the price of survival named and declined.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Section
chapters.summary: Meridian Section is formally dissolved; hearings begin. Sebastian testifies under his real name, Daniel Reeve, then burns his remaining copy of the roster — the trainees deserve anonymity, not exposure. POV: Daniel. Beat: catharsis; truth served without vengeance.

chapters.title: A Man Who Sleeps
chapters.summary: Months later, Daniel and Ilse meet quietly in a coastal town. He sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. No debts remain — except the one they owe each other, freely chosen. POV: Daniel. Beat: resolution; identity, loyalty, and peace finally aligned.
